rules.title: Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) Medical Necessity
rules.rule_text: CPT 27447 (Total knee arthroplasty) is covered when the patient has documented severe osteoarthritis with: (1) radiographic evidence of joint space narrowing, (2) failure of conservative treatment for at least 3 months including physical therapy and/or NSAIDs, (3) significant functional impairment documented. Claims should include supporting ICD-10 codes M17.0-M17.12.
rules.summary: TKA requires documented OA, failed conservative treatment, and functional impairment.
fraud_indicators: High volume of 27447 without supporting documentation
Lack of pre-operative conservative treatment claims
Same patient receiving multiple TKAs in short timeframe

rules.title: TKA Billing Frequency Standards
rules.rule_text: Total knee arthroplasty (CPT 27447) is a major surgical procedure. A provider performing TKA at rates significantly above peer specialty averages (>2 standard deviations) should be reviewed for potential upcoding or unbundling. Normal specialty benchmarks show TKA comprising 20-25% of orthopedic surgery claims.
rules.summary: TKA rates >2 SD above peers require review for upcoding.
fraud_indicators: TKA billed without associated pre/post-operative care

rules.title: Upcoding - General Definition
rules.rule_text: Upcoding occurs when a provider bills for a more expensive service than was actually provided. This includes: (1) billing a higher-level E&M code than documentation supports, (2) billing for a more complex procedure when a simpler one was performed, (3) systematic pattern of billing at highest reimbursement levels. Statistical outliers (>2 SD from peers) warrant investigation.
rules.summary: Upcoding is billing for more expensive services than provided.
fraud_indicators: Procedure mix inconsistent with patient acuity

rules.title: Anti-Kickback Referral Patterns
rules.rule_text: The Anti-Kickback Statute prohibits offering, paying, soliciting, or receiving anything of value to induce referrals. Suspicious referral patterns include: (1) sudden shift in referral concentration to single provider, (2) referral rates inconsistent with patient needs, (3) referrals outside normal geographic or specialty patterns. Changes in referral concentration >50% within 6 months warrant investigation.
rules.summary: Sudden referral concentration shifts may indicate kickback arrangements.
fraud_indicators: Financial relationship between referrer and recipient

rules.title: E&M Level 4 Documentation Requirements
rules.rule_text: CPT 99214 (Office visit, established patient, moderate complexity) requires: (1) moderate level medical decision making, OR (2) 30-39 minutes total time on encounter date. Documentation must support either MDM complexity or time spent. Providers billing 99214 at rates >50% of E&M encounters should be reviewed.
rules.summary: 99214 requires moderate MDM or 30-39 minutes documented time.
fraud_indicators: Time not documented when billed by time

rules.title: E&M Level 5 Documentation Requirements
rules.rule_text: CPT 99215 (Office visit, established patient, high complexity) requires: (1) high level medical decision making, OR (2) 40-54 minutes total time. High MDM requires 2 of 3: (a) 4+ diagnoses/treatment options, (b) moderate+ data review, (c) high risk of morbidity. Providers with 99215 rates >15% of E&M require documentation audit.
rules.summary: 99215 requires high MDM complexity or 40-54 minutes documented.
fraud_indicators: Patient population doesn't support high complexity

rules.title: Phantom Billing Detection
rules.rule_text: Phantom billing involves billing for services never rendered. Indicators include: (1) billing without patient contact, (2) services to deceased patients, (3) services during patient hospitalization elsewhere, (4) impossible service volumes (>24 hours of services billed per day), (5) services to patients with no other healthcare utilization.
rules.summary: Phantom billing is charging for services never provided.
fraud_indicators: No other healthcare claims for patient

rules.title: Doctor Shopping - Controlled Substances
rules.rule_text: Doctor shopping involves patients seeking controlled substances from multiple providers. Indicators: (1) patient visiting 4+ providers for same condition, (2) multiple providers prescribing opioids/controlled substances, (3) excessive pain management procedures without improvement documentation, (4) travel to distant providers bypassing local options.
rules.summary: Multiple provider visits for controlled substances indicates possible shopping.

rules.title: Unbundling - Separate Billing for Bundled Services
rules.rule_text: Unbundling occurs when providers separately bill for services that should be billed together under a single code. CCI edits define bundled services. Same-day claims for related procedures by same provider should be reviewed for proper bundling. Example: billing E&M separately from procedure when E&M is included.
rules.summary: Unbundling is separately billing services that should be combined.
fraud_indicators: E&M billed with procedure lacking modifier

rules.title: Facet Joint Injection Medical Necessity
rules.rule_text: CPT 64493 (facet joint injection) requires: (1) documented facet-mediated pain, (2) failure of conservative treatment, (3) diagnostic confirmation. Frequency limits apply - typically no more than 4 sessions per spinal region per year. Providers with high facet injection volumes require medical necessity review.
rules.summary: Facet injections require documented pain and failed conservative treatment.

rules.title: Provider Ring Detection
rules.rule_text: Provider rings involve collusion between multiple providers to defraud payers. Indicators: (1) closed referral loops between small provider groups, (2) shared patient populations with unusual referral patterns, (3) coordinated billing pattern changes, (4) financial relationships between ring members, (5) high anomaly scores across multiple connected providers.
rules.summary: Provider rings show coordinated suspicious patterns across connected providers.

rules.title: Duplicate Claim Detection
rules.rule_text: Duplicate claims involve billing multiple times for the same service. Detection criteria: (1) same patient, same date, same procedure, same provider, (2) claims submitted to multiple payers for same service, (3) resubmission of previously paid claims. Duplicate claim rates >5% warrant investigation.
rules.summary: Duplicate claims bill the same service multiple times.

patterns.name: Upcoding Ring Pattern
patterns.description: Multiple providers in referral relationship with one provider showing significant upcoding patterns. Referring providers shift referral concentration to upcoding provider.
detection_criteria: Primary provider CPT concentration >2 SD above peers
Referral concentration shift >50% in recent months
High anomaly scores across connected providers

patterns.name: Phantom Billing Pattern
patterns.description: Provider billing for services to patients with no other healthcare utilization or verifiable contact.
detection_criteria: High claim volume relative to documented capacity

patterns.name: Doctor Shopping Pattern
patterns.description: Patients visiting multiple providers for controlled substances or pain management.
detection_criteria: Patient visiting 4+ providers for similar services
High concentration of pain management codes
